# contabo_ptr_record (Resource)

Manage the reverse DNS (PTR) record of an IP address assigned to your account. IPv4 addresses always have a PTR record, so creating this resource updates the existing record and destroying it leaves the record unchanged. For IPv6 addresses the record is created and deleted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Configure your Contabo API credentials
provider "contabo" {
  oauth2_client_id     = "[your client id]"
  oauth2_client_secret = "[your client secret]"
  oauth2_user          = "[your username]"
  oauth2_pass          = "[your password]"
}

data "contabo_instance" "mail" {
  id = "12345"
}

# Reverse DNS for the IPv4 address of an instance.
# IPv4 PTR records always exist: this updates the record, and destroying the
# resource leaves the current value in place.
resource "contabo_ptr_record" "mail_ipv4" {
  ip_address = data.contabo_instance.mail.ip_config[0].v4[0].ip
  ptr        = "mail.example.com"
}

# Reverse DNS for an IPv6 address of an instance.
# IPv6 PTR records are created and deleted with the resource.
resource "contabo_ptr_record" "mail_ipv6" {
  ip_address = "2001:db8:1234:5678::25"
  ptr        = "mail.example.com"
  ttl        = 3600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip_address` (String) The IPv4 or IPv6 address the PTR record belongs to.
- `ptr` (String) The host name the IP address resolves to, e.g. `mail.example.com`.

### Optional

- `ttl` (Number) The time to live of the PTR record in seconds. Can only be set for IPv6 addresses, defaults to `86400`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The identifier of the PTR record, which is the IP address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# PTR records can be imported by IP address
terraform import contabo_ptr_record.mail_ipv4 203.0.113.10
```
